You are a senior QA engineer comparing two test suites for the same healthcare application called Virtual Clinic. SUITE A was generated from the SRS (what the system SHOULD do). SUITE B was generated from the code (what the system ACTUALLY does). === SUITE A — SRS-BASED TEST CASES (excerpt) === ## Virtual‑Clinic – System‑Level End‑to‑End Test Suite **Purpose** – Verify that the complete “Virtual Clinic” solution works correctly for all actors (Admin, Patient, Doctor, Lab‑In‑charge, Chemist) and satisfies the functional and non‑functional requirements described in the SRS (sections 2.1‑2.7). **Scope** – The test cases below exercise **whole‑system flows**, not unit‑level details. They cover the main business processes, error‑handling, security/privacy, performance, scalability and usability expectations. > **Notation** > * **TC‑ID** – unique identifier (e.g., TC‑F‑01, TC‑N‑02) > * **Type** – **F** = Functional, **N** = Non‑functional, **S** = Security/Privacy, **U** = Usability. > * **Priority** – P1 (must), P2 (should), P3 (nice‑to‑have). > * **Traceability** – reference to SRS clause(s) that the test validates. --- ### 1. Core Business‑Process Test Cases | TC‑ID | Title | Preconditions (Setup) | Test Steps (Action) | Expected Result (Pass Criteria) | Post‑conditions | Priority | Type | SRS Trace | |-------|-------|-----------------------|----------------------|--------------------------------|-----------------|----------|------|-----------| | **TC‑F‑01** | **Patient Registration – Successful** | • System up and reachable (Web UI).
• No existing account for email **john.doe@example.com**. | 1. Open registration page.
2. Fill mandatory fields (name, DOB, address, pin‑code, phone, email, password).
3. Submit. | • Confirmation message “Registration successful”.
• Patient record created in Patient DB.
• Email sent (optional). | Patient is logged in (session created). | P1 | F | 2.2, 3.1 (UC‑01) | | **TC‑F‑02** | Patient Registration – Validation Errors | Same as TC‑F‑01, but leave required fields blank / enter invalid email / password < 6 chars. | 1‑3 as above with bad data. | • Inline validation messages for each faulty field.
• No record created. | System unchanged. | P1 | F | 2.2 | | **TC‑F‑03** | Patient Registration – Duplicate Email | Existing patient with email **john.doe@example.com**. | Attempt registration with same email. | • “Email already registered” error.
• No duplicate record. | System unchanged. | P1 | F | 2.2 | | **TC‑F‑04** | Admin – Add New Speciality | Admin logged in, system in “setup” mode. | 1. Navigate to *Admin → Manage Specialities*.
2. Click **Add**, type “Dermatology”, save. | • Speciality appears in list.
• DB table **Specialities** gets new row. | New speciality available for doctor‑speciality linking. | P1 | F | 2.2, UC‑02 | | **TC‑F‑05** | Admin – Link Doctor to Speciality | Admin logged in; Doctor **Dr. A** exists, Speciality “Cardiology” exists. | 1. Go to *Admin → Doctors*.
2. Edit Dr. A, select “Cardiology”, save. | • Doctor record updated with speciality_id.
• Doctor appears in Cardiology doctor list. | Doctor ready to receive Cardiology requests. | P1 | F | 2.2, UC‑03 | | **TC‑F‑06** | Admin – Update Lab Details | Admin logged in; Lab ** === SUITE B — CODE-BASED TEST CASES (excerpt) === **Test‑Case Suite for the *Virtual Clinic* models** *(Only the models present in the supplied `models.py` are exercised. No views, forms or URLs exist in the provided code, therefore no test cases target those components.)* --- **TC-ID** : TC‑CODE‑001 **Title** : Verify `Speciality.__str__` returns the speciality name **Target** : Model – `Speciality` **Preconditions** : - Django test database is ready. **Test Steps** : 1. Create a `Speciality` instance with `name="Cardiology"` and any description. 2. Call `str(instance)`. **Expected Result**: The string returned is exactly `"Cardiology"`. **Test Type** : Functional --- **TC-ID** : TC‑CODE‑002 **Title** : `Speciality` field length enforcement (boundary) **Target** : Model – `Speciality.name` / `Speciality.description` **Preconditions** : - None. **Test Steps** : 1. Attempt to create a `Speciality` with a `name` of 51 characters (exceeds `max_length=50`). 2. Save the instance. **Expected Result**: Django raises a `DataError` / `IntegrityError` on save because the field length exceeds the defined limit. **Test Type** : Boundary --- **TC-ID** : TC‑CODE‑003 **Title** : Verify `Symptom.__str__` returns the symptom name **Target** : Model – `Symptom` **Preconditions** : None **Test Steps** : 1. Create a `Symptom` with `name="Headache"` and any description. 2. Evaluate `str(symptom)`. **Expected Result**: Returns `"Headache"`. **Test Type** : Functional --- **TC-ID** : TC‑CODE‑004 **Title** : `Location.__str__` returns the address field **Target** : Model – `Location` **Preconditions** : None **Test Steps** : 1. Create a `Location` with `address="123 Health St"` (other fields can be dummy). 2. Call `str(location)`. **Expected Result**: Returns `"123 Health St"`. **Test Type** : Functional --- **TC-ID** : TC‑CODE‑005 **Title** : `Hospital` links correctly to a `Location` (OneToOne) **Target** : Model – `Hospital` / `Location` relationship **Preconditions** : None **Test Steps** : 1. Create a `Location` instance. 2. Create a `Hospital` with `location` set to the previously created `Location`. 3. Retrieve `hospital.location` and compare to the original `Location`. **Expected Result**: The retrieved location is the same object (identical primary key). **Test Type** : Functional --- **TC-ID** : TC‑CODE‑006 **Title** : `Hospital.__str__` returns the hospital name **Target** : Model – `Hospital` **Preconditions** : None **Test Steps** : 1. Create a `Hospital` with `name="City Hospital"`. 2. Evaluate `str(hospital)`. **Expected Result**: `"City Hospital"` **Test Type** : Functional --- **TC-ID** : TC‑CODE‑007 **Title** Compare the two suites and produce a structured gap report with these sections: ───────────────────────────────────────── 1. IMPLEMENTATION GAPS (In Suite A but NOT in Suite B) These are requirements that the SRS specifies but the code does not implement. For each gap: state the requirement, what was expected, what is missing in code. ───────────────────────────────────────── 2. UNDOCUMENTED FEATURES (In Suite B but NOT in Suite A) These are things the code implements that the SRS never mentioned. For each: state the feature, which file/function implements it. ───────────────────────────────────────── 3. AGREED COVERAGE (In both Suite A and Suite B) List the areas where both suites agree — these are well-covered. ───────────────────────────────────────── 4. COVERAGE METRICS - Total test cases in Suite A : X - Total test cases in Suite B : X - Implementation gaps found : X - Undocumented features found : X - Agreed coverage areas : X ───────────────────────────────────────── 5. TOP 5 CRITICAL GAPS Ranked by risk to the system. One sentence per gap explaining the risk.
